verses.text: Then all the Israelites from Dan to Beersheba, and from the land of Gilead, came out together as one and gathered before the LORD at Mizpah.
The leaders of all the people of the tribes of Israel took their places in the gathering of God's people. There were four hundred thousand soldiers on foot, armed with swords.
The people of Benjamin heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah. Then the Israelites said, "Tell us how this terrible thing happened."
So the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, said, "My concubine and I came to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
During the night the men of Gibeah came after me and surrounded the house, planning to kill me. They raped my concubine, and she died.
I took her body, cut it into pieces and sent one piece to each region of Israel's land, because they had done this evil and shameful thing in Israel.
Now, all you Israelites, speak up and tell me what you have decided."
All the people stood up together as one and said, "None of us will go home. Not one of us will return to his house.
This is what we will do to Gibeah: we will go up against it as the lot decides.

We will take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, a hundred from every thousand, and a thousand from every ten thousand, to get supplies for the army. Then, when the army arrives at Gibeah in Benjamin, it can punish them for all the shameful things done in Israel."
So all the men of Israel gathered together against the city, united as one man.
The tribes of Israel sent men all through the tribe of Benjamin, saying, "What is this terrible crime that was done among you?
Now hand over those wicked men of Gibeah so that we can put them to death and remove this evil from Israel." But the people of Benjamin would not listen to their fellow Israelites.
Instead, they came from their towns and gathered at Gibeah to fight against the Israelites.
That day the people of Benjamin gathered twenty-six thousand swordsmen from their towns, besides seven hundred chosen men from those living in Gibeah.
Among all these soldiers there were seven hundred chosen men who were left-handed. Each of them could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.
Not counting Benjamin, Israel gathered four hundred thousand swordsmen, all of them trained fighters.
The Israelites went up to Bethel and asked God, "Which of us should go first to fight against the people of Benjamin?" The LORD replied, "Judah will go first."
The next morning the Israelites got up and camped near Gibeah.
The Israelites went out to fight the people of Benjamin and took up battle positions against them at Gibeah.
The people of Benjamin came out of Gibeah and killed twenty-two thousand Israelites on the battlefield that day.
But the men of Israel encouraged one another and again took up their positions where they had stood on the first day.

The Israelites went up and cried before the LORD until evening. They asked the LORD, "Shall we go up again to fight against our relatives, the people of Benjamin?" The LORD answered, "Go up against them."
So on the second day the Israelites went near to attack Benjamin.
This time, when the people of Benjamin came out from Gibeah to meet them, they killed another eighteen thousand Israelites, all of them armed with swords.

Then all the Israelites, the whole army, went up to Bethel. There they sat crying before the LORD. They went without food that day until evening and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to the LORD.
And the Israelites asked the LORD what to do. In those days the covenant box of God was there,

and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, served before it. They asked, "Shall we go up again to fight against our relatives, the people of Benjamin, or should we stop?" The LORD answered, "Go, because tomorrow I will give them into your hands."
Then Israel set men in hiding all around Gibeah.
On the third day they went up against the people of Benjamin and took up positions against Gibeah as they had done before.

The people of Benjamin came out to meet them and were drawn away from the city. They began to kill some of the Israelites as before, about thirty men, in the open field and on the roads, one leading to Bethel and the other to Gibeah.
The people of Benjamin said, "We are beating them as before." But the Israelites said, "Let us run away and draw them away from the city onto the roads."
All the men of Israel moved from their places and took up positions at Baal Tamar, and the Israelites in hiding rushed out of their places west of Gibeah.
Then ten thousand of Israel's best men attacked Gibeah. The fighting was very hard, and the people of Benjamin did not realise that disaster was close.
The LORD defeated Benjamin in front of Israel. That day the Israelites killed twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin, all armed with swords.
Then the people of Benjamin saw that they were beaten. The men of Israel had given way before Benjamin, because they were counting on the men they had hidden near Gibeah.
Those who had been hiding rushed suddenly into Gibeah, spread out and killed everyone in the city with the sword.
The men of Israel had agreed with those in hiding that they would send up a great cloud of smoke from the city as a signal.

Then the men of Israel would turn around in the battle. The people of Benjamin had begun to strike down the Israelites, about thirty of them, and they said, "We are beating them as in the first battle."
But when the column of smoke began to rise from the city, the people of Benjamin turned and saw the smoke of the whole city going up into the sky.
Then the men of Israel turned on them, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, because they saw that disaster had come on them.
So they ran from the Israelites toward the desert, but they could not escape the battle. And the men of Israel who came out of the towns cut them down there.
They surrounded the people of Benjamin, chased them and easily trampled them down in the area east of Gibeah.
Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, all of them brave fighters.

The rest turned and ran toward the desert to the rock of Rimmon. But the Israelites cut down five thousand men along the roads. They kept chasing them as far as Gidom and struck down two thousand more.
In all, twenty-five thousand men of Benjamin who carried swords fell that day, all of them brave fighters.
But six hundred men turned and ran into the desert to the rock of Rimmon, where they stayed four months.
The men of Israel went back to Benjamin's land and put all the towns to the sword, including the people, the animals and everything else they found. They set fire to every town they came to.
